name: Casa Soberanes

dates.altered: An exterior wood stair from the south corner of the veranda has been removed and replaced with a wooden wall; the rear exterior wall has been sheathed in horizontal siding (survey). Restored by Jean Booth and Reuben Serrano in the 1920s-30s (Wikipedia).
dates.note: The survey says 'Built in the later 1830's by Jose Estrada' and cites Kirker's view that no two-storey adobe can date before about 1836; Wikipedia prints 'Built in 1842 by Custom House official Rafael Estrada'. Two dates and two given names on the record; neither changed. The exemplar year is the survey's decade, given as 1838 with this note.

survey.prepared: Historic American Buildings Survey, National Park Service, Western Office, Division of Design and Construction, 450 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco (as the cover reads); the report is a 'Photograph-Data Book Report'; no author or date legible in the extract, which cites a February 1964 periodical.

quotes.text: The Soberanes Adobe (technically Estrada-Soberanes) is one of the fine two-story adobe houses which constitute the chief domestic architectural glory of Monterey. Built in the later 1830's by Jose Estrada, it passed to the Soberanes family in i860; its present owner, Mrs. Mayo Hayes O'Donnell, has presented the house as an historic monument to the State of California (state Historical Landmark No. 712), retaining lifetime use.
quotes.page: 'ARCHITECTURAL AND HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE', page 1 of the report (headed 'CAL-1892 1'); two extract spans overlapped at 'one of the fine two-story adobe houses which constitute the' and are joined at the overlap.

quotes.text: Characteristically, the house has the extremely thick walls, wood door and window frames and tile roof of most Monterey houses of the pre-American period; and like the Larkin house (proto- type of the area), it has a second story veranda.
quotes.page: Page 1 of the report; no further marker in the span.

quotes.text: Typical of the more "progressive" adobes of the l830's (Kirker - California's Architectural Frontierj pp. 13-19 - feels that none of the two-story adobes can date before about 1836), the Estrada- Soberanes adobe is a long, low-slung building with wood balcony- veranda on the second story of its principal (east) elevation. Built of local adobe bricks, with thirty-three inch walls at the base, the house reflects those much older building traditions of Spanish and Mexican California which produced most of the structures prior to the American Period.
quotes.page: 'ARCHITECTURAL INFORMATION', printed after the marker 'HA35 GAL-1892 Page 4' (CAL-1892 Page 4).

quotes.text: The main roof is canti- levered out over the veranda on rafter extentions without fascia or gutter; the overhang is roofed with shakes.
quotes.page: Page 4 or after; no further marker in the span.

quotes.text: There are wood lintels over the, door openings, providing access to the second floor bedrooms from the veranda, Windows in the first floor are double-hung with eight panes in the upper sash and twelve in the lower. The door opening at the northeast has a wood lintel, but windows have plain moldings framing the glassed area.
quotes.page: Page 4 or after; no further marker in the span.

quotes.text: The thick adobe walls occasion deeply splayed interior openings from room to room, with a two-step change of level from front reception rooms to rear dining room, kitchen, etc. The ceilings are of beams and boards on the first floor; the second floor ceilings are of painted wood boards.
quotes.page: Page 4 or after; no further marker in the span.
